items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1961-04-07
items.q: Because Celestine and I both left, you see. I don't think they ever got that band together anymore.

ctx.x: Did you have certain licks that the people really liked better than others that would really bring a cheer from the crowd, so to speak?

That kind of style was good. Now we played, we had a number, Pooinelli, we called it, you see. And there wasn't nobody playing it but us. None of us, they didn't know where we got it and how it like that. And that was a very big hit for us. Pooinelli was a big hit for us. Marilyn was a big hit for us. And a few more others that you could call, you know, but Huinelli, it was, the tune was H-O-Y-E, you see, like that. And Huinelli. And we used to play it, and it was very good. And we would put a break into it, you…
Did you have any licks on the trombone that used to bring a cheer from the crowd? Well, I don't know.

items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1961-04-07
items.q: If they'd come to me and want to play an old funeral or something like that, I'd send them to him... And if they wanted a dance or or anything like that, he would send them to me. And that's how we got along. And whatever it was, well, we'd split the difference.

ctx.x: He was with you in what band? Tuxedo. Orchestra or brass band? No, in both.

Both, huh? Both. Now, you see, the orchestra, that was my band. I'm taking care of that, the dancing. And the Millard and Herbert band was Celestand. See, he didn't bother the orchestra and I didn't bother the orchestra. If they'd come to me and want to play an old funeral or something like that, I'd send them to him. I see. And if they wanted a dance or or anything like that, he would send them to me. And that's how we got along. And whatever it was, well, we'd split the difference. But they were the same men…
Somebody had to go out there and it all?
